market.conclusion: The tech market is moving sideways rather than in an uptrend. QQQ closed at $690.38, below its 50-day average but above its 200-day, and only 22% of stocks are above their 50-day average. This calls for patience: buy quality businesses slowly and make few short-term entries.
arguments: Macro is neutral: fear is normal (VIX 19.46) and credit spreads are steady. I agree this gives no strong push either way.
Lower yields help. The 10-year fell 0.36 points in 4 weeks, which eases pressure on highly valued tech. I count this as a mild support, not a reason to buy.

Leadership has moved away from tech. XLK trails SPY by 7.17 points over 20 sessions while health care and consumer stocks lead, and QQQ lags SPY by 4.0 points. I weigh this heavily against chasing tech bounces.
Breadth is weak at 22%, and trading conditions are YELLOW with 3 of 5 checks passing. Wednesday's rally (QQQ up 2.31%) is not enough to call a turn.
Quant has no validated evidence (0 of 161 forecasts scored), so I give it no weight.
market.change_mind: A QQQ close above $707.23 with breadth improving would make me more willing to enter tech swings. A close below $659.72 would make me more defensive, even on the long-term buys.

deep_dive.case_for: It is a grade A business with revenue up 105.85% year on year in the latest quarter. Its forward P/E is 11.08, and at $173.73 the price sits below its whole value range ($196.49–$411.04). RSI of 28.7 shows it is oversold after a 21.5% drop over 20 sessions.
deep_dive.case_against: The chart is in a downtrend below every average, and earnings on 2026-11-17 can gap the price through any level. The operating margin of 65% is at the top of its 5-year range. Unpaid customer bills are up 127% against sales up 106%, and insiders sold $946.6M outside pre-set plans.
deep_dive.decides: The 2026-11-17 report decides it: whether margins and customer payments hold up, and whether support at $162.81 survives the reaction. For the long term, buy in pieces before and after the report rather than all at once.
